findings.issue: Rejected promises are cached forever: a single transient API failure poisons the in-memory cache for that URL for the life of the server process (or browser session), with no recovery path.
findings.suggestion: Wrap with .catch that removes the entry (`hit.catch(() => cache.delete(url))`) or store resolved values instead of promises, so a retry is possible.

findings.issue: The `error` result of useAsyncData is discarded; any non-404 API failure renders the 'Not found' page and returns HTTP 404, masking server errors (same pattern in abilities, moves and types pages).
findings.suggestion: Destructure `error`, render/throw it distinctly (e.g. `createError({ status: 500 })` or an error state) and only treat a `null` load result as 404.

findings.issue: useAsyncData key interpolates route.params.name, but the key is fixed at setup; on client-side param change the watched refetch writes the new Pokémon's data under the old key, polluting the payload cache.
findings.suggestion: Use a stable page-level key (e.g. 'pokemon-page'); the `watch` option already handles refetching.

findings.issue: Dead export: spriteUrl is never used; PokemonCard.vue:16 re-derives the sprite URL inline, so the helper and the template can drift.
findings.suggestion: Delete spriteUrl or use it from PokemonCard.

findings.issue: buildIndex re-issues the exact fetches getTypes already performed; correctness is saved only by the promise cache, making the layering fragile if the cache changes.
findings.suggestion: Have getTypes expose its records or reuse one shared fetch of the 18 type records in buildIndex.

findings.issue: Near-duplicate of speciesCardsForRefs (pokeapi.ts:217), differing only by carrying a hidden-ability flag.
findings.suggestion: Extend speciesCardsForRefs with an optional transform/flag parameter and reuse it here.

findings.issue: `Promise<any>` plus ~40 `any` casts across the data layer and page loaders defeat the typed interfaces defined in the same file, and package.json has no vue-tsc to catch it.
findings.suggestion: Type the api() helper generically and add vue-tsc (and a lint) to devDependencies with a typecheck script.

findings.issue: compatibilityDate '2025-07-15' is several releases behind the installed Nuxt 4.6.x, silently opting out of newer framework behaviour fixes.
findings.suggestion: Bump compatibilityDate to match the current Nuxt release the app is built with.

findings.issue: The base-URL resolution mixes a build-time-baked runtimeConfig value with a server-only process.env override and a serialised useState — three mechanisms for one config value.
findings.suggestion: Rely on Nuxt's runtime config env convention (NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL) or resolve the override once in a Nitro plugin/server util instead of on every composable call.

summary: A competent, recognisably idiomatic Nuxt 4 app that follows the framework's current patterns (app/ srcDir, useAsyncData+watch, documented setResponseStatus 404 recipe) with a well-bounded shared data layer. The blocking items are operational fragility, not structure: failed API promises are cached forever and API errors masquerade as 404s because useAsyncData's error is ignored. After one round of those fixes plus `any`/dead-code clean-up, I'd merge it.
